# A lambda parameter that happens to share the handler's parameter name is its
# own binding. The handler's event was substituted by name, so every identifier
# spelled the same was replaced: `e > 1` inside the lambda emitted
# `e2.target > 1`, comparing a DOM node property against an int.

sngl generate --platform=html --out=out app.sngl

# The lambda's parameter stands for itself.
grep 'filter\(\(e2\) => e2 > 1\)' out/index.html
! grep 'e2.target' out/index.html

# The handler's own event still resolves to the DOM event.
grep 'state.name = e.target.value' out/index.html

-- app.sngl --
import . "sngl:std"

component main {
    var xs list<int> = [1, 2, 3]
    var n int = 0
    var name = ""
    input(value=name, @input(e) { name = e.value; n = xs.filter(func(e int) => e > 1).length() })
    text(value="{n}")
}
